about.title: American Canyon Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall injuries in American Canyon happen in grocery stores, apartment complexes, and businesses along Broadway and American Canyon Road, often from spills, uneven pavement, poor lighting, or ice that was never cleaned up. California law puts the burden on the injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn people. That's why what happens in the minutes after a fall matters: photos of the exact spot, witness names, and a written incident report can make or break a claim later. Surveillance footage from many businesses is erased on a short cycle, sometimes within days, so preserving it quickly is critical. We handle slip and fall claims on a contingency basis, meaning we only recover a fee if you do. Our team can start gathering evidence and dealing with the property owner or their insurer while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why American Canyon Residents Choose Us

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: Under California law, you generally have to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. We can help track down maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many American Canyon stores and apartment buildings overwrite surveillance footage within days. A quick legal request to preserve that video can be the difference between a supported claim and no evidence at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you were partly at fault for the fall, with your share of fault reducing rather than eliminating compensation. We can help present the facts fairly so your portion of fault isn't overstated by an insurer.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in American Canyon?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a government-owned property, like a public building or sidewalk, have a much shorter deadline. Because American Canyon sits at the intersection of city, county, and Caltrans-maintained areas along routes like Rt 29, it's worth confirming who owns the property early. Waiting too long can cost you the right to pursue a claim at all.

items.question: What if the store says they didn't know about the spill?
items.answer: That's actually the central legal question in most premises cases, whether the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. Evidence like how long the spill sat there, prior complaints, or cleaning schedules can show the owner had time to notice and fix it. We can help gather that evidence before it disappears.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We handle slip and fall claims on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation to get your free case review.
